extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and exercises defining and developing separatedness, quasiseparatedness, varieties, normalization/finite morphisms, and related results (graphs, cancellation, Reduced-to-Separated) in scheme-theoretic algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of integral closure (Theorem 9.7.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose A is a Noetherian integral domain, K = K(A), L/K is a finite field extension, and B is the integral closure of A in L. (a) If A is integrally closed and L/K is separable, then B is a finitely generated A-module. (b) If A is a finitely generated k-algebra, then B is a finitely generated A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: Reduce (a) to the Galois case; use a K-basis b1,...,bn of L, form the matrix M with ij-entry σ_i(b_j), show det M (call d) is Galois-fixed and use adjugate tricks to show d^2 ci ∈ A so B is contained in a finitely generated A-module. For (b) use Noether Normalization to reduce to A = k[x1,...,xn], reduce to normally closed extensions and purely inseparable cases, ultimately showing B is finite over k[x1,...,xn]. Warning: part (b) fails for general Noetherian A; the integral closure of a Noetherian ring need not be Noetherian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization is finite in important cases (Exercises 9.7.M, 9.7.5 remarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an integral finite type k-scheme, then its normalization ν : X' → X in a finite field extension (or in a finite separable field extension when X is normal) is a finite morphism. In particular, normalization of a variety (including in a finite field extension) is a variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise: show normalization morphism is finite under the stated hypotheses; combined with Theorem 9.7.3 and Noetherian hypotheses this gives finiteness. See also sketch proof techniques referenced in 9.7.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization morphism is birational and an isomorphism generically (Exercises 9.7.N, 9.7.O, 9.7.P)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an integral finite type k-scheme, then the normalization morphism is birational. The normalization map of X is an isomorphism on an open dense subset of X. If ρ : Z → X is a finite birational morphism from an irreducible variety to an irreducible normal variety, then ρ is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints given: use Proposition 6.5.7 for birationality, Proposition 6.5.5 for isomorphism on dense open, and exercise chains; these facts show normalization does not change the generic point and is generically an iso.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagonal morphism is locally closed (Proposition 10.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any morphism π : X → Y of schemes, the diagonal morphism δ : X → X ×_Y X is a locally closed embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: cover Y and X by affines Vi and Uij, describe the diagonal on these affines and show it is a closed embedding locally; this observation underpins the definition of separatedness and the use of the diagonal in arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of separated morphism (Definition 10.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y is separated if the diagonal morphism δ_π : X → X ×_Y X is a closed embedding. Equivalently, the image ∆ is a closed subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separatedness is the scheme-theoretic analog of the Hausdorff condition; it is a property of morphisms (and thus of schemes relative to their structure morphism). Many consequences follow from checking the diagonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separatedness examples and non-examples (Exercises 10.1.B–D, 10.1.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Locally closed embeddings (in particular open and closed embeddings) are separated. Every morphism of affine schemes is separated. The line with doubled origin is not separated (its diagonal image is not closed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises guide hands-on checks and counterexamples; use these to test understanding of the diagonal criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective space over a base is separated (Proposition 10.1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The structural morphism P^n_A → Spec A is separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two proofs: (1) direct affine-coordinate calculation checking the diagonal restrictions are closed embeddings on overlaps; (2) conceptual proof factoring the diagonal via Veronese and Segre embeddings (closed embeddings). Use either method to show projective space is separated and thereby deduce quasiprojective schemes are separated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Proposition on diagonals and intersections (10.1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If U and V are open subsets of an A-scheme X, then ∆(U ∩ V) ≅ U ×_X V (i.e., restrictions of the diagonal identify with the intersection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for local arguments and the 'magic diagram' interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of variety over a field k (10.1.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A k-variety is a reduced, separated scheme of finite type over k. (Some sources also require irreducibility; often assume k algebraically closed.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subvariety = reduced locally closed subscheme; open/closed subvarieties explained. Morphisms of k-varieties are automatically finite type and separated (Exercise 10.1.L).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection of affine opens in separated morphisms (Proposition 10.1.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X → Spec A is a separated morphism and U, V are affine open subsets of X, then U ∩ V is affine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: on a separated scheme over an affine base, intersections of affine opens are affine (this simplifies Cech cohomology arguments). Warning: this property does not characterize separatedness (counterexamples exist, e.g., doubled origin over a point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiseparated morphisms (redeﬁnition 10.1.9 and exercise 10.1.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y is quasiseparated if the diagonal δ_π : X → X ×_Y X is quasicompact. For affine targets, this is equivalent to: for affine U,V ⊂ X mapping to Spec A, the intersection U ∩ V is a finite union of affines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separated ⇒ quasiseparated. Many common morphisms (e.g., morphisms from locally Noetherian schemes) are quasiseparated. Quasiseparatedness is preserved by base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separatedness and quasiseparatedness: stability properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Separatedness and quasiseparatedness are preserved by base change (Prop.10.1.10), are local on the target (Prop.10.1.11), and are closed under composition (Prop.10.1.13). Products of separated/quasiseparated morphisms are separated/quasiseparated (Prop.10.1.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These closure properties allow checking these conditions after base change, on local patches, and combining morphisms; proofs rely on behavior of diagonals under base change and composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphs of morphisms and rational maps (Definitions 10.1.17, 10.2.4 and Prop.10.1.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: For π : X → Y over Z, the graph Γ_π = (id,π) : X → X ×_Z Y is a locally closed embedding; if Y is separated over Z, Γ_π is a closed embedding; if Y is quasiseparated then Γ_π is quasicompact. For a rational map π : X ⇢ Y (X reduced, Y separated) define Γ_π as the scheme-theoretic closure of the graph of any representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graph properties follow from base change of the diagonal. For rational maps, the graph is independent of representative (exercise) and often provides a way to resolve indeterminacy (e.g., blow-ups).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation Theorem for a property P of morphisms (10.1.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P be a class of morphisms preserved by base change and composition. Given a commutative square X --π--> Y --ρ--> Z with τ : X → Z ×_Y (something) in P and δ_ρ (the diagonal of ρ) in P, then π is in P. Corollaries: if locally closed embeddings are in P and τ is in P then π in P; if closed embeddings are in P and ρ is separated then π in P; similarly for quasicompact/quasiseparated variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem is applied by taking graphs and using base change; useful to deduce properties of π from properties of τ and ρ via the diagonal. Many familiar consequences (injectivity/surjectivity cancellation in Sets) illuminate the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universally injective morphisms and diagonal criterion (10.1.20, 10.1.P)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π : X → Y is universally injective iff the diagonal δ_π : X → X ×_Y X is surjective. Universally injective morphisms are separated. For finite type schemes over an algebraically closed field k, universally injective ⇔ injective on closed points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These equivalences allow testing universal injectivity via the diagonal and closed points in finite type/algebraically closed settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced-to-Separated Theorem (10.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two S-morphisms π, π' : U → Z from a reduced scheme U to a separated S-scheme Z that agree on a dense open subset of U are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: the locus V where they agree is a closed subscheme containing a dense open subset; on a reduced scheme the only closed subscheme with dense underlying set is the whole scheme. Consequences: rational maps from reduced sources to separated targets have a largest domain of definition; rational functions have maximal domains; uniqueness/extension results follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locus where two morphisms agree (Exercise 10.2.A and remarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two morphisms π, π' : X → Y over Z, there is a largest locally closed subscheme V ⊂ X on which π and π' agree; V is closed if Y is separated over Z. The locus can be nonreduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct V as the fiber product with the diagonal (π,π')^(-1)(∆). Use as a universal property: any µ:W→X on which π∘µ = π'∘µ factors uniquely through V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of maps on closed points for k-varieties (Exercise 10.2.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For k-varieties, two morphisms π, π' : X → Y that agree on closed points (i.e., π(p)=π'(p) for every closed point p of X) are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This shows that classical varieties embed fully faithfully into k-schemes; exercise asks to generalize to non-algebraically-closed fields appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph of a rational map is independent of representative (Exercise 10.2.E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of the graph of a rational map π : X ⇢ Y (with X reduced, Y separated) via scheme-theoretic closure of a representative's graph is independent of the chosen representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to the case where one representative has domain equal to X and show the scheme-theoretic closure of the graph in X × Y is X ×_Y closure = whole Γ_π.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational maps: largest domain and indeterminacy locus (10.2.3 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational map from a reduced scheme X to a separated scheme Y has a largest domain of definition (union of all domains where it is a morphism). The complement is the locus of indeterminacy; points there are fundamental points. Graphs and blow-ups can be used to resolve indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Reduced-to-Separated to see uniqueness; Example: rational function on A^2_k given by (x,y) ↦ [x,y] to P^1 has domain A^2_k \ {(0,0)}. Exercises point to blow-up constructions making rational maps honest morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of extending maps over effective Cartier divisors (Exercise 10.2.G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a Z-scheme, Y a separated Z-scheme, and D ⊂ X an effective Cartier divisor, any Z-morphism X \ D → Y can be extended to X in at most one way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to affine case Spec A and show scheme-theoretic image considerations (vanishing of a section t) force uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated-to-Separated theorem (Exercise 10.2.H)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two S-morphisms from a locally Noetherian scheme U to a separated S-scheme Z that agree on a dense open subset containing the associated points of U are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalizes Reduced-to-Separated; the presence of the associated points replaces reducedness for the uniqueness argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universally closed morphisms and preliminary notion of properness (10.3 intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes π : X → Y is universally closed if for every base change Z → Y the map X ×_Y Z → Z is closed (i.e., sends closed sets to closed sets). Properness will be introduced as an analog of topological properness (preimage of compact is compact) and characterized using universally closed plus additional hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section begins the development leading to projective schemes being proper; keep in mind the base-change stability in the definition of 'universally P' properties.
